findings.evidence: Preface, Reading conventions, Cross-references: "A section reference takes the form § N.M ... which means Chapter N, Section M — so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4". However §7.3 appears at page 136 (Ch 7 opening) as "the whole-slot floor of 17 KV-resident requests" and at page 137 as "The canonical concurrency ceiling is that resident-basis quotient floored to a whole slot — 17" — neither instance is preceded by an explicit 'Ch. 7 §' within the same sentence. The convention says bare §N.M 'names Chapter N, Section M' but §7.3 numerically means Ch 7, Section 3, which is the Worked Example section — the concurrency ceiling content actually lives in §7.3 as numbered. Reading §7.3 as 'Ch 7, Section 3' is correct; reading it as 'Section 7.3 of the current chapter' is also correct only because these instances are inside Ch 7.
findings.issue: Bare '§7.3' references (pages 136, 145) do not include the chapter prefix 'Ch. 7' at first mention in those sentences, creating ambiguity with the Preface convention that '§ N.M' means Chapter N Section M (where §7.3 → Ch 7, Section 3, not section 7.3 of an unknown chapter). The instances are unambiguous only because they occur within Ch 7 itself.
findings.fix_instruction: At first mention within each chapter, write 'Ch. 7 § 3' instead of bare '§7.3' to avoid ambiguity, per the Preface's own stated convention.
